condition: suspected acute central retinal artery occlusion presenting with abrupt complete monocular visual loss in the right eye while reading small print
level_rationale: Abrupt complete loss of all sight in the right eye occurring 20 minutes ago while reading in a 71-year-old woman indicates suspected acute central retinal artery occlusion or acute retinal vascular ischemia—an ocular stroke equivalent requiring immediate emergency hospital stroke and ophthalmic evaluation—whereas noticing letters have looked slightly blurry through the right eye over 8 months while reading small print reflects gradual non-emergent refractive or media change warranting a routine outpatient physician or eye evaluation.

Suddenly lost all vision in the right eye 20 minutes ago

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain older-adult lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntactic-frame by clinical/everyday lexical crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + uncontracted causal belief-addition clause (-att) + Rule A first-choice same-eye chronic blur outpatient control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (71-year-old woman, reading small print at home, and sudden complete loss of vision in the right eye 20 minutes ago) with zero apostrophe contractions ('Im', 'I am', 'it is'), a 1-word span difference (10 vs 9 words), and zero diagnosis labels ('central retinal artery occlusion' omitted). Keeping 'my right eye' identical in f3 avoids widening the body site while Rule A first-choice progression/severity change to 8 months of slightly blurry letters through the right eye shifts care cleanly from emergency hospital stroke/eye care (level 4) to routine outpatient evaluation (level 2) with zero stated negatives.
